name: Elephas
desc: Biotech company applying cancer biology and AI to immunotherapy diagnostics, including tumour tissue testing to match patients to cancer drugs.
markets: Based in Wisconsin, serving cancer researchers and drug developers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Early-stage diagnostics biotech with a clinical audience; F1 offers little marketing value.

name: Eve
desc: AI-native platform for plaintiff law firms handling case intake, document review, drafting and discovery in personal injury cases.
markets: Customers are plaintiff law firms in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Niche legal software for US law firms; F1 hospitality is of limited use for its buyers.

name: Framer
desc: Website builder and design tool that lets designers create, publish and host professional sites visually, with AI page generation.
markets: Used by freelancers, startups and enterprises worldwide; headquartered in Amsterdam.
rationale: Design-led brand with a worldwide creative audience; F1 offers visibility to designers and startups, and a design showcase.

name: Husk Power Systems
desc: Rural energy company operating solar minigrids in India and Africa, selling power and equipment to villages and small businesses.
markets: Founded in India; operates solar minigrids in India and Africa, with a US headquarters listed.
rationale: Rural energy developer with social-impact focus; F1 sustainability messaging is possible, but marketing budget is small.

name: Inspur Computer Technology
desc: Designer of servers, storage and cloud computing hardware for data centres, as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Inspur Group.
markets: Sells servers to cloud and data-centre customers in China and overseas; Inspur group has been subject to US trade restrictions.
rationale: Large server maker with some export sales; F1 offers technology showcase, but US restrictions and Chinese ownership complicate partnerships.

name: LILT
desc: AI-powered enterprise translation, localisation and content creation service combining machine translation with human review.
markets: Enterprise customers localise content for many languages, mainly in North America; wider operations are not confirmed.
rationale: Translation vendor serving global brands; F1 offers worldwide audience and hospitality, and its customers' brands span many countries.

name: Omnidian
desc: Provider of performance protection plans for residential and commercial solar systems and batteries, covering monitoring, repairs and production guarantees.
markets: Customers are homeowners, installers and developers in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Solar services brand with US homeowner and installer audience; F1 sustainability themes offer limited fit for its customer base.

name: Quo
desc: Business phone app giving teams shared numbers, calls, texts, voicemail and AI call summaries, aimed at small businesses and startups.
markets: Customers are small businesses and startups, mainly in the United States; international reach is not confirmed.
rationale: Small-business phone app with modest marketing scale; F1 is a costly fit for its customer base.

name: Reka AI
desc: AI research and product company building multimodal foundation models that understand text, images, video and audio.
markets: Founded by researchers from major AI labs; customers and international operations are not confirmed from the line.
rationale: Foundation model developer seeking enterprise awareness; F1 offers an AI technology showcase, but commercial scale is small.

name: Ripcord
desc: Robotic digitisation company converting paper records and documents into searchable digital data for enterprises, utilities and government.
markets: Customers are enterprises, utilities and government bodies, mainly in the United States; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Document services for large organisations with little brand marketing need; F1 offers limited value.

name: Safe Security
desc: Cyber risk management platform that quantifies cyber risk in financial terms for boards and security teams using AI.
markets: Founded in India; customers in the United States, India and other regions, with offices in several countries.
rationale: Cyber risk vendor selling to boards and insurers; F1 offers hospitality for senior buyers, and insurers and security firms partner with F1.

name: Tennr
desc: Healthcare AI startup whose automation platform processes referrals and patient intake paperwork, reading faxes and routing them to clinics.
markets: Customers are specialty healthcare practices in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Narrow healthcare administration software with US-only buyers; F1 offers little marketing value.

name: TigerGraph
desc: Graph database and analytics platform for deep link analysis of connected data, used for fraud detection and supply chain.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia use its graph platform.
rationale: Data platform for enterprises; F1 offers a data-heavy technology showcase and hospitality, though marketing budget is moderate.

name: Wandercraft
desc: Developer of self-balancing exoskeletons, including Atalante and Eve, that let people with paralysis stand and walk, used in rehabilitation centres.
markets: Founded in France; devices used in rehabilitation centres in Europe and the United States.
rationale: Robotics medical device with a strong human story; F1 offers technology showcase and awareness, though customers are clinics.

name: Well
desc: Health technology company providing healthcare access tools, including digital communications for providers and patients; identity is not fully confirmed.
markets: Based in North Carolina; customers are healthcare providers and organisations in the United States; wider operations are not confirmed.
rationale: Healthcare communications software with narrow buyers; F1 fit is weak and the company identification is uncertain.

name: Xelix
desc: Finance software that uses AI to automate accounts payable controls, detect duplicate payments and errors and reconcile supplier statements.
markets: Customers are large finance teams in the United Kingdom, Europe and the United States.
rationale: Finance software vendor selling to multinationals; F1 offers hospitality for CFOs, and finance brands are prominent F1 partners.

name: Zeitview
desc: Drone-based inspection and analytics provider with an AI platform for solar farms, roofs, wind turbines and utilities.
markets: Network of certified pilots operates across several countries, serving solar, wind and utility customers.
rationale: Inspection analytics for energy assets; F1 sustainability and aerial-technology themes give some fit, though customers are B2B.

name: LangChain
desc: Company behind the open-source LangChain framework and the LangSmith and LangGraph tools for building applications and agents on language models.
markets: Developers worldwide use its open-source framework; enterprise customers include firms in several regions.
rationale: Developer-focused AI brand with global community; F1 offers an AI technology showcase, though marketing is developer-led.

name: Alianza
desc: Cloud communications platform that telecom operators use to deliver voice, messaging, video and business phone services under their own brand.
markets: Operator customers mainly in the United States and Latin America; wider reach is not confirmed.
rationale: Telecom software sold to operators; F1 offers limited marketing value, though Latin America is a major F1 market.

name: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)
desc: Non-profit research institute founded by Paul Allen doing open AI research and building tools such as OLMo language models.
markets: Research institute based in Seattle; outputs are released openly to researchers worldwide.
rationale: Non-profit research body with no commercial marketing aim; sponsorship is very unlikely.

name: ANYbotics
desc: ETH Zurich spin-out making the four-legged ANYmal robot that autonomously inspects industrial sites, reading gauges and detecting leaks.
markets: Customers in energy, oil and gas and industry across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Robotics brand with industrial customers worldwide; F1 offers engineering showcase and hospitality for energy executives.

name: Ataccama
desc: Data management software offering a data trust platform for data quality, governance, catalogue and master data management with AI automation.
markets: Czech roots with a Boston headquarters; enterprise customers in North America and Europe.
rationale: Enterprise data brand seeking wider awareness; F1 offers a data technology showcase and hospitality for data leaders.

name: AtScale
desc: Analytics company selling a semantic layer platform between data warehouses and BI tools, giving enterprises one governed definition of metrics.
markets: Customers are large enterprises, mainly in the United States; international reach is not confirmed from the line.
rationale: Data analytics vendor with enterprise buyers; F1 offers data technology showcase and hospitality, though marketing scale is moderate.

name: Austal
desc: Australian shipbuilder and defence contractor designing and building aluminium and steel vessels, including patrol boats, ferries and US Navy ships.
markets: Shipyards in Australia and the United States; customers include the US and Australian navies and ferry operators.
rationale: Listed shipbuilder with mostly defence customers; F1 offers limited marketing value, and naval work restricts brand-led sponsorship.

name: Clear Labs
desc: Biotechnology company using genomics and automation to provide food safety and microbial testing based on next-generation sequencing.
markets: Customers are food producers and testing laboratories, mainly in the United States; international operations are not confirmed.
rationale: Testing technology for food producers; F1 offers limited marketing value for a small B2B brand.

name: DroneDeploy
desc: Cloud platform helping organisations plan drone flights, capture and map aerial imagery and robot data for construction, mining and energy.
markets: Customers in construction, mining, energy and agriculture across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Aerial data brand with international B2B customers; F1 circuit and construction use cases offer a technology showcase.

name: Flywheel
desc: Data management and analysis platform for biomedical imaging research, serving hospitals, universities and pharmaceutical companies.
markets: Customers are research hospitals, universities and pharma firms, mainly in the United States; international reach is not confirmed.
rationale: Research data platform with narrow academic and pharma buyers; F1 fit is weak.
